item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Building 14: The Building 14 page no longer gives 1941 as its build year
item.description: The Building 14 page no longer gives 1941 as its build year. The 2013 Historic Preservation Commission memo says both 1941 and 1944, the National Register form says 1941, and the Port's 2019 memo says 1944 in its text and 1941 in its table. Source: Port memo to the Historic Preservation Commission, Nov 26, 2013 (default.sfplanning.org/meetingarchive/planning_dept/commissions.sfplanning.org/hpcpackets/2013.1168E.pdf); NRHP registration form (npgallery.nps.gov/GetAsset/99f11ae6-3834-4f99-840a-0e8a097398e6); Port Calendar Item 12A, Jan 4, 2019 (sfport.com/media/4465/download).

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Building 14: The sources disagree on when Building 14 was built (1941 or…
item.description: The sources disagree on when Building 14 was built (1941 or 1944; the Port and city documents print both) and on when its rehabilitation began, and the page now says so. The architect credit now rests only on the magazine article that names the design team for the Historic Core buildings. Source: Port Commission staff report Item 12A, 2019-01-04 (https://www.sfport.com/media/4465/download); HPC informational memo, 2013-11-26 (https://default.sfplanning.org/meetingarchive/planning_dept/commissions.sfplanning.org/hpcpackets/2013.1168E.pdf); NRHP registration form NRIS 14000150 (https://npgallery.nps.gov/GetAsset/99f11ae6-3834-4f99-840a-0e8a097398e6); National Trust for Historic Preservation, Winter 2016 (https://savingplaces.org/stories/transitions-saved-pier-70-historic-core); Bisnow, 2017-04-19 (https://www.bisnow.com/san-francisco/news/office/historic-pier-70-leases-130k-sf-to-single-tenant-73464); STRUCTURE magazine (https://www.structuremag.org/article/pier-70-building-113-114-renovation/).

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Building 14: The summary and facts no longer merge two courtyards: the…
item.description: The summary and facts no longer merge two courtyards: the planning packet says Buildings 113-116 and 14 frame a 45,000 sq ft courtyard, while the National Register nomination separately has Building 14 and Building 2 forming one. Building 14 is no longer called the smallest of the eight Historic Core buildings. The 'first occupancy this summer' item is dated 2017, not 2018, and is described as a Capital Planning Committee presentation. The map notes now say the old Assessor lots (4052001, 4111003) were retired in 2018 and that the building falls within an active lot with no address, and the source list drops an unsupported OEWD publisher and an author affiliation. Source: SF Planning, Historic Preservation Commission informational packet, case 2013.1168E, 2013-11-26 (https://default.sfplanning.org/meetingarchive/planning_dept/commissions.sfplanning.org/hpcpackets/2013.1168E.pdf); National Park Service, Union Iron Works Historic District National Register nomination, 2014-04-17 (https://npgallery.nps.gov/GetAsset/99f11ae6-3834-4f99-840a-0e8a097398e6); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 12A staff report, 2019-01-04 (https://www.sfport.com/media/4465/download); Port of San Francisco, Pier 70 SUD presentation to the Capital Planning Committee, 2017-09-11 (https://onesanfrancisco.org/sites/default/files/2019-05/Agenda%20Item%206-%20Pier%2070%20IFD%20Presentation.pdf); DataSF Parcels (https://data.sf.gov/d/acdm-wktn).

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Building 14: Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation receives a… (~2023)
item.description: Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation receives a Governor's Historic Preservation Award (~2023). Source: California Office of Historic Preservation, 2023.

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Building 14: Port staff update to the Commission (memo dated Jan… (Jan 4, 2019)
item.description: Port staff update to the Commission (memo dated Jan 4, 2019): six of eight buildings complete, Buildings 101 and 102 still under construction, project 100% subleased except two atrium retail spaces; whole-Historic-Core project total costs (not the cost of this building alone) rose from $81.9M at 2014 approvals to $127.0M in Table 2's '2018, Actual' column, while the memo's text gives 'an estimated $125 million at project completion in 2020'; Table 2 marks one line (Building 102's $6.7M) as a future-expenditure estimate (Jan 4, 2019). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04.

item.title: Under construction · Pier 70 Building 14: Master lease approved by the Board of… (~Jul 2015)
item.description: Master lease approved by the Board of Supervisors and fully executed in July 2015, giving Orton site control; the Port memo says construction commenced thereafter, and the National Trust's Winter 2016 issue says the rehabilitation 'began this past September' (year not printed; a 2017 Bisnow article says 2014 – see open questions) (~Jul 2015). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04; National Trust for Historic Preservation (Katherine Flynn), 2016.

item.description: Built as the Heavy Warehouse for equipment used in Machine Shop 1 and ship outfitting (1941 in the NRHP nomination and in tables in the Port's and the Historic Preservation Commission's documents; the prose of those two documents says 1944) (~1941). Source: National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17; Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04.
